newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Passport battle ends with tea party in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Passport battle ends with tea party in Hong Kong.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten on Monday laid to rest a long, bitter dispute over British passports when he threw a tea party for widows of local servicemen who fought for Britain in World War Two.
The party, at Patten's residence at Government House, was to celebrate the awarding of full British passports, including the right to live in Britain, to some 40 widows and wives of servicemen.
"It's been the end of a long story, but it has ended happily and successfully," said Patten, who will sail out of Hong Kong on July 1 when the British colony of over 150 years returns to China.
Guests included Jack Edwards, chairman of the Royal British Legion, who had fought more than 30 years for benefits for war veterans and those they left behind.
The emotional issue has long festered in Hong Kong and it was not until last year when Britain finally agreed to allow the elderly women full British citizenship.
Many of Hong Kong's 6.4 million people hold only British travel documents that do not give them right of abode.
